renderer: headless Chromium, SwiftShader (software) — costs rank the parts of a frame, they do not predict a GPU
pacing: off in an automated browser — these are drawing costs, not paced rates
method: each build loaded alone, zoomed out by wheel events to the same scales (N 226 Solar System, N ≈ 272–276 Local Group, N 290 the whole universe), frames counted over 8 s; then in the new build the frame cost with the glass saving off and on (HCC_PERF.cost, mean of two runs each), and the same frame drawn both ways in one task and read back (HCC_PERF.wallCheck)

cost.note: before = the same build with HCC_PERF.oneWall(false): two-sided glass, no veil fold

wall_note: differences are the rounding of near-invisible layers in an 8-bit buffer (done once instead of dozens of times) and, where something bright lies inside the horizons, the old sort that blended the far wall OVER it: the veil now lies behind everything inside it
